identity.title: Stable Video Infinity: Infinite-Length Video Generation with Error Recycling

problem.claim: Generate non-looping, ultra-long videos with stable visual quality, per-clip prompt control, and multimodal conditioning.

gap.claim: Existing anti-drifting approaches are limited to single-prompt extrapolation and tend to produce homogeneous scenes with repetitive motion; the authors also identify a mismatch between clean-data training and autoregressive inference on error-prone outputs.

contributions.claim: Stable Video Infinity (SVI), incorporating Error-Recycling Fine-Tuning to use self-generated errors as supervisory prompts for error identification and correction.
A closed-loop recycling process that injects historical errors, estimates residual errors efficiently, and banks them in timestep-aware replay memory for resampling.
A video-generation approach designed to scale from seconds to infinite durations without additional inference cost while supporting audio, skeleton, and text conditions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Error-Recycling Fine-Tuning as a new type of efficient training that recycles the DiT's self-generated errors into supervisory prompts.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SVI scales videos from seconds to infinite durations with no additional inference cost and remains compatible with audio, skeleton, and text streams.
The authors report evaluation on three benchmarks spanning consistent, creative, and conditional settings, describing the results as verifying versatility and a state-of-the-art role.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper introduces SVI for stable, non-looping ultra-long video generation with per-clip prompts and multimodal controls.
It contrasts SVI with existing anti-drifting methods, which the authors say remain single-prompt and visually repetitive.
The authors frame the deeper issue as a training–inference discrepancy: clean training inputs versus autoregressive self-generated errors at test time.
Error-Recycling Fine-Tuning closes this gap through closed-loop error injection, residual-based estimation, and replay-memory banking across timesteps.
The authors report long-duration scaling, multimodal compatibility, and evaluation across consistent, creative, and conditional benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The paper explicitly connects a deployment-time distribution mismatch to a training procedure that recycles model-generated errors as supervision.

lessons.interpretation: When inference feeds model outputs back into the model, training on clean inputs alone may omit the states that drive failure.
lessons.application: For an autoregressive system, define a closed-loop training path that injects representative historical errors and uses the resulting deviations as replayable supervision.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when deployment inputs are not autoregressively generated or when storing and sampling error states is impractical.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide benchmark names, metrics, baselines, quantitative results, or the operational meaning of “infinite” duration.
The stated no-additional-inference-cost and state-of-the-art claims lack decisive conditions and numerical evidence in the supplied units.
